coupling.rationale: Narrow interfaces, explicit shared state (URL query), and clean server/client separation with graceful no-JS fallbacks; only minor seams: the view→api import and the magic element ids.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:32-52 — pokemonRefsToSpecies uses a generic `source` passthrough so the ability page gets `is_hidden` without boolean flags — designed around the real variation
app/src/lib/templates.ts:6-12 — CardData's optional `types`/`note` model the two genuine card variants; cardList stretches to every list unchanged
app/src/lib/templates.ts:44-49 — section() standardizes the region-landmark pattern used by every detail page
app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:57-66 vs abilities/[name].ts:36-45 vs types/[name].ts:39-48 — the loader/404-status/title-fallback/template triad is copy-pasted verbatim in four routes
app/src/lib/format.ts:1-38 — display rules (humanize, dexNumber, latestEnglishFlavorText, orDash) centralized instead of inlined per page
abstraction_design.rationale: The domain abstractions genuinely stretch (an Items section would reuse api/data/format/templates wholesale), with the only real copy-paste being the modest per-route 404 scaffold, which is arguably the framework's own shape.

findings.issue: The abortable fetch → DOMParser → replaceWith fragment-swap helper is duplicated with the same error-fallback logic in pokemon/[name].client.ts:54-70; a fix to one (e.g. script execution, focus handling, error UX) will miss the other.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared `swapFragment(url, id, signal)` helper into src/lib/ (a client module) and use it from both custom elements.

findings.issue: The detail-page scaffold — `if (!data) responseInit.status = 404`, `title: context.props.data?.label ?? 'Not found'`, `if (!data) return notFound()` — is copy-pasted in four routes, so a new resource page (e.g. Items) copies it a fifth time and any change to 404 handling repeats four times.
findings.suggestion: Factor a `defineResourceRoute({ load, title, template })` helper (or at least a shared `resourceDocument(context)` and 404-status helper) so the pattern lives once.

findings.issue: The isBuildRender guard that prevents API fetching during Gracile's asset-collection build render must be remembered in every route handler (6 call sites); a new route that forgets it will fetch and embed API data at build time, silently violating the spec's live-data requirement.
findings.suggestion: Centralize the guard — e.g. wrap handlers in a shared `withBuildRender` helper, or move the check inside the api()/data.ts loaders so it is impossible to skip.

findings.issue: The presentation layer imports spriteUrl (which reads process.env.API_BASE_URL) from the transport module lib/api.ts, mixing view concerns into the API client.
findings.suggestion: Move mediaUrl/spriteUrl into their own lib/media.ts (or a constants module) so templates depend on a URL helper, not the caching HTTP client.

findings.issue: Client enhancement scripts are coupled to server markup via magic ids (`moves-tables`, `results`, `moves`) and form field names, an implicit contract that breaks silently if the template is edited.
findings.suggestion: Export the fragment ids as named constants from a module both the server template and the client script import, making the contract explicit and greppable.

findings.issue: All styles for all pages live in one global 564-line stylesheet (organized only by MARK comments), so adding or removing a page means editing a long shared file and carries collision risk in team edits.
findings.suggestion: Split into per-route CSS (Gracile supports colocated route/document CSS) or at least per-page files imported from document.css.

findings.issue: The app ships zero tests of its own; the pure helpers here (humanize, latestEnglishFlavorText, orDash, pokemonRefsToSpecies) are exactly the invariants future edits will rely on, yet only the acceptance suite guards them.
findings.suggestion: Add a few unit tests for format.ts and data.ts mapping logic to give refactorings a safety net beyond the Playwright acceptance run.

findings.issue: The stylesheet link is wired via `new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname` rather than the documented source-path form (`href="/src/..."`), making the asset pipeline non-obvious and upgrade-sensitive.
findings.suggestion: Use the framework-documented link href (or import the CSS through Gracile's documented channel) and verify output after framework upgrades.

summary: This is a cleanly layered, idiomatic Gracile app where the seams are in the right places: one card renderer, one species-resolution helper, one API/cache module and one shared URL contract mean most edits are single-point. The costs are small but real: the client fragment-swap logic and the per-route 404 scaffold are duplicated, the build-render guard must be remembered per route, and all CSS is one global file. Extending it (an Items section) reuses the whole lib layer but copies the route boilerplate.
